key_insight: DiffSequence-Q uses quantum auxiliary supervision during training to improve protein generation conditioned on secondary structure and solubility, while keeping generation entirely classical.
engineering_relevance: The hybrid design lets quantum prediction heads influence a Transformer denoiser without requiring quantum execution during sequence generation.
method: Condition multinomial diffusion on per-residue secondary structure and a continuous solubility target.
Jointly optimize diffusion loss and auxiliary solubility prediction loss using a QNN or QKAN head over shared Transformer representations.
Generate protein sequences through classical reverse diffusion.
evidence_signal: On CATH, DiffSequence-Q led four evaluated models in secondary structure recovery for complete generation; the best QNN and QKAN configurations achieved 14.0% and 22.7% higher mean predicted solubility than the MLP baseline, respectively, and selected proteins showed experimental biological activity across three families.
watch_item: Solubility gains were measured by a separate prediction model, and the abstract does not establish quantum computational advantage or specify quantum hardware requirements.
paper_title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
